column1: # Hand-authored mnemonics, one per compound kanji.
# Read by tools/build_kanji_components.py, which checks that every line here
# actually uses each of its kanji's component keywords and warns about any
# that don't. A kanji with no line here falls back to the mechanical
#   * Name every component by the keyword it carries in
#     component-keywords.tsv, spelled exactly the same way, so a learner
#     meets the same word for that shape everywhere it appears.
#   * Say where the parts sit — above, below, beside, inside, wrapped
#     around, hanging over. The arrangement is half of what is being learnt.
#   * Land on the kanji's own meaning. One or two sentences, no more.
#   * Written from the component keywords and nothing else. No mnemonic
#     source was consulted for any line in this file — see

column2: A person has stopped beside a tree, back against the bark. That is what rest looks like.
A lid clamped down over eight: squash two out and six is what is left.
One slash laid across ten, and ten swells into a thousand.
Evening falls, too dark to see a face, so the mouth underneath calls out a name.
An enclosure with legs kicking about inside it — four walls, four legs, four.
One flat line resting on top of someone big: even the biggest of us has sky above.
A child under a roof, bent over a desk, practising one character at a time.
A lid, and under it a cut scratched into the surface. That scratch is writing.
The sun is already ten hands above the horizon, so you are up early.
Trees on the left, measure on the right: pace out the trees and you have a village.
A tree on the left, mix on the right: wooden desks where children mix together all day. School.
One tree standing over a whole grove below it — a forest.
Steam curling round a cut in the lid — the invisible spirit rising out of the pot.
A rice field, and beneath it the strength that works it: the man in the fields.
Rice fields on the left, a nail on the right, pinning them into neat blocks. A town.
One stroke laid on top of white: a hundred blank pages waiting.
Craft a hole wide enough and what is left above you is empty sky.
Grass on top, and underneath it change: grass that has changed into a flower.
Grass on top and early below — grass is up first thing every morning.
An eye up on two legs, walking about to see.
An eye with eight little legs scuttling under it: a shellfish.
A mouth above, stop below. The foot carries you and knows when to halt.
A sprout below the moon takes on a cold blue.
Stand up in the sun and let out a sound.
A lid over father, and the whole household gathers underneath to mingle.
One person standing above a cloud of others — a meeting.
A person beside their own origin: the body you started out in.
A person on the left, can on the right. A person asking whether they can — what?
A person who suddenly starts making things.
Two lines resting on a pair of legs: stand up straight at the beginning.
A mouth up on legs, telling you what to do. Your elder brother.
Small sparks scattered over something lofty: light.
Eight arms prying open what is private below, and it becomes public.
A winter's foot dragging over two chips of ice.
Eight above, a sword below. Everything gets cut into parts.
Seven strokes beside a sword: cut.
One hand reaching round to clasp another hand inside it. Friends.
A story ten mouths have passed along — it has to be old by now.
Something private held up over a mouth: set it on a pedestal.
An open box enclosing one mouth, and everyone in it says the same thing.
A mouth inside an enclosure, going round and round: one more time.
Small cuts scratched inside an enclosure. That is a map.
A jewel walled up inside an enclosure: a country.
An enclosure you stroll around in a long robe. The garden.
Earth on the left, a snake sliding over it on the right: the ground.
Earth with sunbeams falling across it — an open place.
Evening on the left, fortune-telling on the right: read the omens outside.
Big already, and one dot more underneath. Plump.
A woman not yet grown: your younger sister.
The woman who takes you to market. Your elder sister.
Arrive under a roof and you have reached the room.
A pig under the roof. That, historically, is a house.
Earth measured out by the inch: the temple grounds.
A mountain sitting on top of a stone. A boulder.
A lid over a cloth stall: the market.
Put down the knife, pick up the broom. You have come home.
A lean-to hanging over something private, with room to spare underneath. Wide.
Divination under a lean-to roof: a shop with a fortune-teller out front.
A bow on the left, a straight line on the right, drawn back. Pull.
Small marks over a hand, and the hand lands on the right one. A hit.
Level lines on the left, hair strokes trailing on the right: shape.
A rice field above a heart, ploughing the same row over and over. Think.
Filial piety on the left, a light strike on the right. That is teaching.
Strike an entangled heap apart and count what falls out. Number.
Sun beside moon. Nothing is brighter.
A little sun that comes to life only at night: a star.
The sun beside the Buddhist temple bell — that is how you tell the time.
Sun beside blue and the weather clears up.
The sun with a pheasant beside it, one bird for each weekday.
A brush above the sun: write until the light goes.
Stop on top, a few more below. Stop, a few more, stop again. Walking.
Water with a snake winding through it: the pond.
Water on the left, steam on the right. Vapour.
Water on the tongue and suddenly you are lively again.
Every drop of water there is, gathered in one place: the sea.
Divination over a fire, and the flame leaves little scorch spots.
A king beside his village, putting everything in its place. Logic.
Divide the rice field below and everyone takes a turn on their strip.
An arrow flying straight out of the mouth: you know it.
An altar beside earth, and everyone in the district belongs to it. A company.
Grain on the left, fire on the right, burning off the stubble. Autumn.
Grain measured out with a dipper and sorted into departments.
Bamboo slips joined together underneath: the answer.
Thread beaten flat for the whole clan to write on. Paper.
Thread laid across a rice field, and every furrow looks thin beside it.
Thread beside a pile of it, braided together into a group.
Threads meeting on cloth: a picture.
Thread running on and on like a spring: a line.
An ear inside the gate, listening to everyone who comes through.
A boat beside the marsh: a ship.
A bending person over a coil, and the colour rises in their face.
Words beside ten: count it out and you have a plan.
Words beside self: write down what happened to you.
Words and a tongue together: a tale.
Words for I, words for you — language.
Words beside sell: read the label before you buy.
A net thrown over shells, and shells are money. Buy.
Earth above, stop below. Run across the ground until you stop.
A road wrapped round an axe, close enough to fetch it. Near.
A road wrapped round a walled path — go straight through.
A road wrapped round a circuit: seven days, and back where you started. A week.
A road wrapping round a neck, leading you on. The way.
A road wrapped round a long robe, the hem trailing off into the distance. Far.
Village on the left, beforehand on the right: what was there before the village. Open plains.
Sun in the gateway, and light in the gap is the interval itself.
Rain above a hand: rain you can hold. Snow.
Rain on top and cloud below, because rain has to come from somewhere.
A bean beside a head, and the head is about that size. The head.
A youth beside a head: the face you look at.
A mouth beside a bird: the chirp.
A sprout above a winter's foot, pushing up through the frost. Barley.
A village over a fire, and the soot turns everything black.
A lid resting on the king below: the master of the house.
A person beside a scholar, attending on them.
A person on the left, a snake on the right — somebody else entirely. Other.
A person beside a stake driven in to mark their place while they are away. A substitute.
A person beside the master of the house, living under the same roof. Dwell.
A person beside an official, sent out on an errand. Use.
A person beside a lineage, holding the thread of it. The one in charge.
A person beside spit, saying it twice over. Double.
One person above the king, and together that is everyone. Whole.
A cover on top, give underneath: copy it out and hand it over.
Bone on the left, knife on the right: laid out in a row.
A pile on the left, strength on the right, shifting it. Help.
Excuse wrapped round strength — no excuse left, so put your back into it. Exertion.
Heavy on the left, strength on the right: move it.
Moon on the left, weary on the right — outlast them and win.
A person beside a spoon, stirred into something else. Change.
A hiding box with a cut inside it, dividing the town into wards.
A hiding box with an arrow inside: pull the arrow out and treat the wound. Doctor.
Earth on top, private below — bury it and it is gone.
An ear on the left, a hand on the right, taking hold of it.
A governor hanging over a mouth, giving the orders. Mister, ruler.
A mouth on the left, not yet on the right: not tasted yet. Flavour.
Grain on the left, a mouth on the right, and everyone fed. Harmony.
A mouth above a shell — one mouth to pay for, one member of staff.
Stand on top, bright below: set out your stall and make a deal.
A mouth inside the gate, calling in a question.
Earth on the left, turn back on the right: too steep, turn back. A slope.
A woman beside a pedestal: everything begins here.
Grain on top, a woman below, entrusted with the harvest.
A roof over measure: guard every inch of what is under it.
A woman under a roof, and the household relaxes.
A roof over a foot, planted and settled. Determine.
A roof over each and every arrival: a guest.
A roof over a spine of linked rooms: a palace.
A roof over a hundred travellers: an inn.
Writing on the left, measure on the right, set opposite each other.
A body hanging over a phrase, hunched at a desk. The bureau.
A body hanging over arrive — you have arrived under the roof. A house.
Cloth on the left, long on the right: a long roll of cloth to write on. A notebook.
A lean-to hanging over a cart: the warehouse it is parked in.
A lean-to hanging over a court: the courtyard.
A stake enclosing craft, and the craft is done the same way every time. A ceremony.
A step on the left, a weapon on the right: marched off on duty.
A step on the left, a Buddhist temple on the right: pace the temple yard and wait.
Self on top, heart below: your own heart, and the breath it drives.
Second above a heart: a heart that comes second. Bad.
Not above a heart: the heart says no. Grief.
Mutual above a heart: two hearts thinking the same thought. An idea.
Sound above a heart: what the heart is trying to say. Meaning.
All above a heart, all at once. Feeling.
A door on the left, an axe on the right — the place they are kept.
A hand on the left, a nail on the right. Strike.
A hand on the left, a weapon on the right, hurled. Throw.
A hand on the left, join on the right: gather it up.
A hand on the left, a Buddhist temple on the right, holding the whole thing steady.
A hand on the left, delicious on the right — the finger that points at the best dish.
Direction on the left, a strike on the right: strike out in any direction. Set free.
An imperial order on top, correct below: everything put in order.
The sun on the left, summon on the right: call the sun out and it shines.
The sun above a person, beating down. Sultry.
The sun on the left, sound on the right — you can hear it but not see it. Darkness.
That on the left, moon on the right: that moon, that date. A period.
A tree on the left, turn back on the right: sawn and turned over. A plank.
A tree on the left, the master on the right: the tree the whole house leans on. A pillar.
A tree on the left, stopping on the right — where the tree stops going down. The root.
A tree on the left, straight on the right: stand it up straight and plant it.
A tree on the left, yellow on the right, felled and lying sideways.
A tree on the left, tall on the right: tall timber laid across. A bridge.
Ice on the left, a yawn on the right — cold and bored, waiting for the next one.
Water on the left, decide on the right: the water has to go one way. Decide.
Water on the left, reason on the right — water that will not mix. Oil.
Water on the left, skin on the right: the skin of the water. Waves.
Water on the left, the master on the right: pour for the master.
Water on the left, eternity on the right: swim on and on.
Water on the left, a sheep on the right, drifting off overseas. The ocean.
Water on the left, a pennant on the right, streaming out. Flow.
Water on the left, resemblance on the right: pour water on it until it no longer resembles itself. Extinguish.
Water on the left, warm on the right. Warm water.
Water on the left, an alley on the right: an alley of water. The harbour.
Water on the left, a barbarian on the right, camped at the water's edge. A lake.
Water on the left, sunbeams on the right, heating it. Hot water.
A mountain above ashes: dig into the hillside and bring out coal.
A cow on the left, not on the right — a cow and not-a-cow, and between them, everything. A thing.
The king on the left, seek on the right: the jewel everyone is chasing. A ball.
A rice field above mediate: something has to sit between the fields. A boundary.
Fire on the left, a rice field on the right: burn it off and it becomes dry field.
Sickness hanging over third: taken ill and third in the queue.
A tent on top, a bean below: climb up to pitch it.
A tree on the left, an eye on the right, looking each other over. Mutual.
Ten above a tool: ten tools all agreeing. True.
An arrow on the left, a bean on the right: as long as an arrow, as short as a bean.
Stone on the left, level on the right: grind it level. Polish.
An altar on the left, a hook on the right, bowing low. A salute.
An altar on the left, state on the right: what is stated at the altar. The gods.
An altar on the left, full on the right: a full jar set at the altar. Blessing.
Grain on the left, few on the right — a few grains through the glass. A second.
A hole on top, nine below: dig nine holes and you are doing research.
Sound above early: the first sound, and the chapter it opens.
Stand above a village: the child standing about in the village.
Bamboo on top, reason below: bamboo with a reason to be hollow. A flute.
Bamboo above a brush: the bamboo handle of the writing brush.
Bamboo above a Buddhist temple: bamboo slips in the temple, all cut to one length. Class, and so forth.
Bamboo above mutual: bamboo sides facing each other. A box.
Thread on the left, reach on the right: how far up the thread you have reached. A grade.
Thread on the left, winter on the right: the thread runs out in winter. The end.
Thread on the left, carve on the right: carved and dyed. Green.
Thread on the left, east on the right: work the thread until the sun is up. Practice.
A sheep above big: a big sheep. Beauty.
Feathers above white: a white-feathered fledgling flapping until it learns.
Old hanging over the sun: someone who has seen many days. A person.
Grass above old: old grass, bitter to chew. Suffering.
Grass above what: grass and what else is on your back? A load.
Grass above the capital: the leaves come down all over town. Fall.
Grass above a flat board: pressed flat. A leaf.
Grass above music: the grass that makes you well enough to sing. Medicine.
Words on the left, a Buddhist temple on the right: words with temple weight. A poem.
Words on the left, a circuit on the right: run the words round until they are in tune.
Words on the left, flames on the right: talk around the fire.
A bending person above a shell: bent under the debt. Defeat.
Run wrapped round self: get yourself up and running.
A foot on the left, each on the right: each foot in turn along the path.
A cart on the left, a cloud on the right, wheels turning like cloud.
A cart on the left, holy on the right: light enough for anyone to pull.
Bend above a dragon: bend your back from dawn. Agriculture.
A road wrapped round turn back: turn back along the road. Return.
A road wrapped round a heap: follow the heaped tracks. Chase.
A road wrapped round a frontier pass: see them off at the pass. Escort.
A road wrapped round a bundle: bundle it up and go. Quick.
A road wrapped round a small bird: birds go forward and never back. Advance.
A road wrapped round roam: wander wherever it goes. Play.
A road wrapped round an army, moving it. Carry, and the luck it takes.
Spit on the left, a village on the right: the village split into sections.
A person on the left, a village on the right: village upon village. The metropolis.
A wine jar on the left, self on the right: pour yourself a cup and hand the rest round. Distribute.
Water on the left, a wine jar on the right. Sake.
Metal on the left, lose on the right: the metal you can afford to lose. Iron.
Metal on the left, stopping on the right: metal one stop below gold. Silver.
Level inside the gate: pull the bar level and the gate opens.
A hill on the left, complete on the right: the completed building on the hill. An institution.
A hill on the left, sunbeams on the right: the sunny side of the hill.
A hill on the left, all on the right — a hill for everybody, cut into steps. A storey.
A small bird above a tree, and then another, and another. Gather.
Correct wrapped round a head: get the heading right. A topic.
Food on the left, a yawn on the right: mouth open. Drink.
Food on the left, an official on the right: the official building where you are fed. A mansion.
A horse on the left, a ruler on the right: horses measured out along the road. A station.
Self above give: the part of yourself that gives you away. The nose.

column2: Small marks under a cover, and a child underneath taking them all in. Study.
A lid over a mouth over something small — a tower stacked up on a hill. The capital.
A person under a roof with one line ruled beneath them: right here, right now.
Ten over an open box with a dry frame inside — a shed turned to face the warm south.
A person over one line over a mouth: lid, seal and jar, all fitting together.
A scholar up on a cover with legs under it — the stall he sells from.
One line laid over self, with a winter's foot dragging below — the season that walks the other way.
A lid pulled over a person still out in the evening. Night.
Eight over condolences with a slash through it — the younger brother, always last in line.
Two bows, each with ice on it. Frozen through and ready to snap. Weak.
A bow on the left, and on the right a private insect that turns out to be stronger than it looks.
A step, a tiny thread, and a winter's foot dragging along behind it.
Stand a tree up and take an axe to it — fresh-cut timber. New.
White with ice either side of it, up on a tree: a rack of bells. Music.
Big brother on the left, a yawn on the right, mouth wide open. A song.
Bamboo over an eye over twenty — counting rods, watched very carefully.
Grass over a person over a tree: leaves picked off the bush. Tea.
Stand by a tree and see — a parent watching from just far enough away.
Rain on top with a sun trapped underneath it, flashing on and off. Lightning.
A table tipped on its side with an insect blown in under it. Wind.
A lid, a mouth, and open country underneath — a tower you can see for miles.
A bending person for a head, a rice field for a body, fire for a tail fin. A fish.
An eye up on eight — a stand with everything laid out on it. Tools.
A claw above, a cover between, a hand below: one hand passing something down to another.
A mouth over one hooked line, calling out a name or a number.
An open box with a slash on top and a mouth inside — a window you turn to face.
A person under one line, a mouth on the left and a seal on the right: an order handed down.
A mountain over a cliff over dry ground — where the land stops and the water starts.
A lean-to hanging over twenty, with a hand underneath measuring them off.
A bending person, a hand, and a heart beneath them all, racing. Hurry.
Twenty over the sun — twenty long days ago, and then a good deal more.
A moon on the left, a seal and a hand on the right: a body with something fitted onto it.
A tree on the left, a sheep over water on the right. That is simply the manner of it.
Stop on top, rice in a container below — a mouthful, and the teeth that stop it.
A tent up top, two lines and a pair of legs below: packed up and setting off.
An eye over something small — a district watched over from above.
A sheep with a slash through it and an eye underneath: you have arrived, and you are being looked over.
A moon over an altar — an offering laid out for the festival.
Bamboo over condolences with a slash through it: slips of bamboo, numbered in order.
A lid over something private over a moon — a child growing up under cover.

column2: One flat stroke, and nothing else. Nothing simpler exists.
A cross with its bottom stroke swinging out to the right, like a 7 tipped over.
Three lines stacked up. Count them and you have your answer.
A stroke standing on the ground line with a tick out to the right: something is up there.
The ground line on top, and a stroke hanging down underneath it.
A box with a line driven straight through the middle of it.
A hook with one leg kicking out from under it — the last number before ten.
Two lines, one short and one long, with nothing at all between them.
A line, a zigzag, a line: scaffolding held between two rails.
Two legs walking and nothing above them. A person, seen head on.
A foot striding out ahead of a pair of legs — out in front, and so earlier.
Two strokes leaning together like the mouth of a tent you duck into.
Two strokes splaying apart. Eight is the number that splits cleanly in half.
A box with two legs dropping out of the bottom of it: the coin, and what it is worth.
Two mountains stacked up, one climbing out of the other.
A bent arm flexing, and nothing else. Pure muscle.
A cross, straight up and straight across. Ten fingers.
An open square. A mouth, held wide.
A hand with a mouth underneath it — the hand you eat with.
A cross planted upright with a line under it: a mound of earth.
A crescent moon just showing itself. Evening.
A person with both arms flung out wide. This big.
A figure with its legs crossed and its arms folded across.
A baby with its arms out and its legs still wrapped up.
One stroke with a tiny fleck either side of it. Small.
Three peaks along one ridge line.
Three lines running downhill side by side. Water on the move.
A hand with a carpenter's square under it — the hand that holds the work steady.
A figure over two crossbars: harvests counted off, one to a year.
Fingers, a wrist, and a hook at the end. A hand held up.
A box with one line across the middle. The sun with a spot on its face.
A tall box with two lines inside, curved down one side like a crescent.
A trunk, branches out to either side, roots spreading below.
A tree with one extra mark ruled across its roots: where the whole thing starts.
Two trees standing side by side. A wood.
A foot stopped square on a line — halted in exactly the right place.
A stream with drops flying off it to either side.
A flame with sparks leaping away on both sides.
A big person with one extra fleck: the dog on the end of the lead.
A king with one extra dot — the jewel he is wearing.
Three ranks — heaven, earth and people — with one line joining all of them.
A shoot pushing up through the ground line. Something alive.
A square divided into four plots. A field seen from above.
The sun with one ray coming off the top of it. Bright, and pale with it.
An eye stood up on its end, pupil and all.
A boulder sitting under an overhanging cliff.
A figure with its arms out, planted on a line. Standing.
Two stalks side by side, each with a leaf drooping off it.
A twist of silk with the loose ends dangling below.
An ear drawn straight down the page, with its ridges marked inside.
A creature with a body and a feeler, curled up small.
Earth over a fire — hot enough to glow.
A cart seen from above: axle down the middle, wheels out to each side.
A roof over the ground with nuggets buried underneath it.
A cloud across the top, and four drops falling inside it.
One sweeping stroke under a lid, running off further than anyone is counting.
Nine with a dot tucked into the crook of it, rolled up into a ball.
An open box with a person tucked in under it.
A single curved blade with a handle. A sword.
A cap over a moon and a blade, the whole thing pushing forward.
Two people standing back to back, turning away from each other and from the cold.
One stroke laid across a stake standing upright: the shadow at its shortest.
Two strokes split off the top and a line straight down the middle. Cut in half.
A cliff with a spring running out from under it — where it all comes from.
A cross-topped figure above a low slab, with the sound carrying out from under it.
Two evenings stacked one on the other. Night after night after night.
Small, with one stroke slicing off the corner. Less even than small.
A beam held between two plates — the carpenter's square that shapes everything else.
The curve of a bow, string and all.
A hook with three flecks scattered round it: a heart, and the beats coming off it.
A single door on its hinge — one half of a gate.
A ten with a stroke swept through it, cut across the grain.
A lid with a flagpole through it, leaning off one way.
Three lines crossed by a sweep, with the sun coming up underneath at last.
A ruler over a sun over a line: the middle of the day, measured out.
Grass with the sun caught in it, and the moon still up beside them. Dawn.
A tree with two extra pairs of branches, all of them leaning towards you.
A sun caught in the branches of a tree — sunrise, so that way is east.
A footprint pressed flat into the ground. That foot is going nowhere.
A figure with its arms wrapped round, and two dots for feeding a baby.
A person above a mother — one after another after another.
Three strokes with a tail flicking off the bottom. A tuft of hair.
Two crossed strokes over two more, like arms folded. Father.
A horned head on a body, seen from the front.
A box with a spine down the middle and two shelves across it. Something built to be used.
A field boxed in, with a line ruled over the top. A picture in its frame.
Ten over an eye over a bent line — look straight down it.
A big figure with its head cut flat: an arrow, flight and all.
Grains scattered off a cross in every direction.
Two wings side by side, each with its feathers marked in.
An old man bent over, with a curl of thought coming out from under him.
An open box with two ribs marked inside it.
An eye with a mark on top — the nose you point at when you mean yourself.
A step on the left and a crossroads on the right. Going somewhere.
A box with legs and a lid: the sun sinking into a basket at the end of the day.
A horn, ridged along its length and tapering to a point.
A mouth with lines of sound stacked up above it.
Two slopes falling away to either side, with a mouth at the bottom of them.
A rice field sitting on the earth. Where people settle.
Long hair over long legs, everything about it drawn out.
Two doors facing each other, both of them shut.
A lid pulled over a heap of good things. Dinner.
Two whiskers over a face — the head, and the neck holding it up.
A mane on top, a body, and four legs flying along underneath.
A crest, an eye, a body, and four toes gripping the branch.
A field boxed in top and bottom, ripening.
A flat top with a stroke hanging straight down from it. A nail, driven in.
Three uprights joined by one long bar — one lifetime laid across the next.
One roof over two matching halves, each with an upright of its own.
A tree with a figure climbing it, one foot out either side.
A hook with a stroke through it and a tail dropping down, all set up in advance.
A hand gripping a brush that runs straight down through everything else.
A cliff with a hand reaching back under it.
Three mouths stacked in a pile. Goods, sorted and counted.
A big figure boxed in at the shoulders — dead centre.
A roof over a cross and two legs: whatever is actually under there.
A roof with layers packed under it and two chips of ice at the very bottom.
A bird perched on a mountain, out in the middle of the sea.
Three rivers with a sandbank marked in each one.
A stroke with two flecks and one long flat bar underneath. Level.
A cross over a stack of bars — good fortune, piled up.
A banner on a pole with people falling in behind it.
A banner on a pole with an arrow beneath it: everyone who fights under the same flag.
A box with two uprights bending up out of the top of it.
A hand reaching over a moon and holding onto it.
A comb of uprights standing over a sheaf of work.
A bare bone on the left and a figure kneeling down beside it.
Water with one extra fleck frozen onto its side.
Water on the left, and on the right a hand reaching down a hole after a tree's roots.
Water on the left, and a tall stack of strokes piled up on the right.
A rice field with one stroke pushing up out of the top of it.
A rice field with a line driven straight through it, top to bottom.
A hand peeling a hide back off its frame.
A dish on its stand seen side on, with the dividers inside it.
Horns on top, and a body ruled into three below them.
A single drop falling into a dish.
A cloak with two bars ruled across the top of it — whatever is on the outside.

Cause above the heart — the kindness that is the cause of it. Grace.
A roof over a net over a heart, everything held under the one rule. The constitution.
A hand on the left, compare on the right, holding two of them up side by side. Criticism.
A hand on the left, daybreak on the right. Shoulder the load at first light: carry.
A hand on the left, one line and abundant on the right, held out flat. Worship.
A hand on the left, wide on the right, spreading it out. Extend.
A hand on the left, a cottage on the right. Walk out of the cottage and leave it: throw away.
A hand on the left, a small bird on the right, pushed off the branch to see where it goes. Infer.
A hand on the left, an army on the right, waving it forward. Brandish.
A hand on the left; on the right the chirping of birds up a tree, every one of them handled. Manipulate.
A stalk on the left, strike on the right, cutting the other side down. The enemy.
The sun on the left, center on the right, throwing the picture up in the middle. Reflect.
The sun on the left, excuse on the right. The sun excuses itself: nightfall.
The sun on the left, lead on to on the right, drawing you out into it. Warm.
Must not, above the sun. The sun must not stay: dusk.
Good on the left, the moon on the right, clear all night. Bright.
A tree on the left, a table on the right. Wood on legs: a desk.
A tree on the left, strike on the right, splitting it into flat sheets. One sheet, two sheets.
Water on the left, nine on the right and a tree underneath — dipped nine times in the dye. Colour it.
A tree on the left, vermilion on the right: the red stump left in the ground, and a share in it.
A tree on the left, observance on the right, held out straight in both hands. A rod.
A tree on the left, must not on the right — a wooden pattern nothing must depart from. A copy.
A tree beside a drum, with a measure on the right marking how far it has grown. A standing tree.
A valley on the left, a yawn on the right. A mouth as wide as a valley: greed.
Water on the left, a marsh on the right. Follow the water round the edge of the marsh: run alongside.
White above water — clean water coming straight up out of the ground. A spring.
Water on the left, before on the right. Water first, before anything else: wash.
Water on the left, to branch on the right, the stream splitting in two. A faction.
Water on the left, adjusted on the right: the crossing made and the debt settled. Finish.
Water on the left, a meadow on the right, and the spring that feeds it. The source.
Water on the left, morning on the right, coming in right on time. The tide.
A cliff hanging over fire, and what is left underneath it. Ashes.
A king on the left and a king on the right with a knife between them — the jade split into equal shares. A squad.
A rice field above together: one field not like the others. Different.
Sickness hanging over a walled path, all the way down it. Pain.
White above a king, the crown catching the light. The emperor.
Turn into, above a dish. The dish turns into a heap: prosper.
Bright above a dish, sworn over the bowl in full daylight. An alliance.
A stone on the left, few on the right. Stone ground down to almost nothing: sand.
Grain on the left, private on the right. The grain that is mine.
Grain on the left, invariably on the right — the store nobody is ever told about. Secret.
A roof over eight, split open underneath. A hole.
A hole up top with private and a heart under it — the gap you look out through. A window.
Bamboo above a rib, fibres running the whole length of it. Muscle.
Bamboo above a thorn: a sharp little slip of bamboo with the plan written on it.
Bamboo above an interval, one slip with a gap either side. Brief.
Rice on the left, China on the right, boiled down sweet. Sugar.
A slash above thread, the whole lot hanging from one end. A lineage.
Thread on the left, craft on the right — thread worked until it comes out deep red. Crimson.
Thread on the left, inside on the right, the bolt of cloth taken in. Settlement.
Thread on the left, barracks on the right: every thread the same, drawn up in rows. Pure.
Thread on the left, a small worm on the right. The worm that makes the thread: silk.
Thread on the left, accompany on the right, one following the other straight down. Vertical.
Thread on the left, an inn on the right, the cloth pulled in for the night. Shrink.
A net above a person: your name caught and written down. The office, and the signature.
Feathers above stand — up on the perch, waiting for tomorrow. The following day.
An ear on the left, a mouth on the right and a king below: hears everything, says it plain. A saint.
A moon on the left, a market on the right, busy day and night. The lungs.
A rice field above a moon — the field inside you where the crop ends up. The stomach.
North above a moon: two people back to back, turned away. The back.
A moon on the left, turmoil on the right, everything churning behind the ribs. The chest.
A moon on the left; on the right small marks over a villain, plotting away. The brain.
A moon on the left, sunbeams on the right, coiled into one long bright loop. The intestines.
A moon on the left, return on the right — the part of you that keeps coming back for more. The belly.
A moon on the left, a storehouse on the right. The body's storerooms: the organs.
A thousand above a mouth, a thousand words out of the one mouth. The tongue.
Grass above right, freshly picked with the right hand. Young.
Grass above a person: a name that stands up out of the field. Renowned, and written down.
Grass above many, the whole bundle held over the pot. Steam.
The heavens above an insect — a gift from the sky that spins thread. The silkworm.
To cut, wrapped round clothes. Cut the cloth to shape: tailor, and judge.
Robust above clothes, dressed up for the part. Attire.
An altar on the left, see on the right. Look at it properly: inspect.
Words on the left, a measure on the right. Take their measure, then go after them: attack.
Words on the left, a direction on the right, taking your words that way. Visit.
Words on the left, a ruler on the right, measured out into another language. Translate.
Words on the left, a director on the right, giving each word its own job. Parts of speech.
Words on the left, intention on the right — writing down what you meant to remember. Records.
Words on the left, endure on the right. Hear it out to the end and admit it: acknowledge.
Words on the left, prolong on the right: the announcement everyone has been waiting for. A birth.
Words on the left, turn into on the right. Words that turn into deeds: sincerity.
Words on the left, give on the right — the wrong words given out. A mistake.
Words on the left, order on the right, set out one after another. An argument.
Words on the left, a person on the right, and then another one. Various.
Awe above words: a warning that makes you sit up. Admonish.
Middle above a shell, carried in the middle of both hands. Precious.
Responsibility above a shell. Take on the job, take the money: the fee.
A road running under stopping, backing away down it. Retreat.
A road running under precious — something valuable dropped along the way. Left behind.
Droop on the left, a village on the right, the post-bag hanging at the village stop. Mail.
Metal on the left, ten on the right: a thin sliver of metal with an eye. A needle.
Metal on the left, small on the right. A small piece of metal: a coin.
Metal on the left, mount on the right. Metal as hard as a hill: steel.
A gate wrapped round talent, barred across. Shut.
A gate wrapped round each floor, one above the next. A tower.
A hill on the left, to descend on the right, coming down it. Fall.
A hill on the left; on the right compare over earth, step matched to step. The palace stairs, and the one at the top of them.
A hill on the left, surplus on the right. Clear the surplus off the slope: remove.
A hill on the left, a badge on the right, blocking the way. Hinder.
A nail on the left, a head on the right. The very top of the head.
Beforehand on the left, a head on the right — handed over ahead of time for someone else to hold. Deposit.

column2: One flat line with a stroke dropping through it and legs splayed either side — a bird that has decided not to land. No.
Two uprights crossed by two horizontals: the wooden frame round the top of a well.
A lid, and underneath it someone kneeling to hear what has just been said. An order.
Two short strokes on the left and a person on the right, one thing held up beside another. By means of.
A person on the left, and on the right something bent right down with a line ruled under it. Low.
A lid on top, a door in the middle and a mouth at the bottom — a shed you can shut. A storehouse.
A person on the left, then an upright, then an arrow: a lookout waiting to see which way the weather turns.
Two legs kicking apart with a mark either side, a crack splitting open. An omen.
Twenty at the top and two legs underneath, holding it up together.
A mouth over a bent stroke on the left and a knife on the right, cutting them apart. Separate.
A neat cap over a rice field with strength under it, chest out and ready. Courage.
A hand reaching down on the left and a kneeling figure on the right. Press it down: a stamp.
A hook wrapped round a single mouth — one voice giving out the orders. The official.
Earth on the left; on the right a person over a dish, boiling a pan dry. Salt.
A big person with one extra line laid across the shoulders. The husband.
A person leaning forward with something slipping off the top stroke. Lose.
A roof, and under it two little humps in a row: the rooms of a government office.
A sheep's head with a slash through it over a worker's hand — two things that do not match. A difference.
A step on the left; on the right a stack of lines over a heart. Virtue.
A heart with a slash driven straight through it. That will happen, without fail.
A halberd with an extra stroke propped inside it: the work is done. Become.
Twenty over a moon on the left, a strike on the right, knocking it all apart. Scatter.
A banner on a pole at the left, streaming out over a stand on the right. A flag.
A tree with a short extra line across the top — the upper branches have not grown out yet. Not yet.
A tree with one long line across the very top: the far tip of the branches. The end.
A tree with a mouth tied round its middle. A bundle.
A rice field sitting up in the branches of a tree. The fruit.
A figure kneeling with its mouth wide open. Something missing, and a yawn: lack.
One curved stroke with a short line hooked under it, like a name cut into a plate. A clan.
The same shape as a clan with an extra stroke driven through it — not one family but all of them. The people.
A line with a hook and four flecks flying off it, hands grabbing from every side. Seek.
Water on the left; on the right grass over two little tangles of thread, growing thicker. Nourish.
A row of uprights over a long line with fire underneath — the whole lot burnt away to nothing.
Thread on the left; on the right a box with a tail hanging off it, twisted into a rope.
A staring eye stood up on its end, watching from the side of the room. The retainer.
A dot on top, then a bowl on a stand. The good stuff, kept at the bottom.
A lid over crossed folds, hanging from the shoulders. Clothes.
Two little horns over a bird on the left, and see on the right. Look hard: a view.
Two wings with their feathers showing, one above the other, lifting away. Fly.
Antlers over a lean-to for a body, and two legs picking their way along underneath. A deer.
A slash with a leg swung under it, propped up and going nowhere. A long time.
A person on the left; on the right a load balanced across a pole. Duty.
A person on the left, and on the right a tree with something small tucked under its top. Keep it safe.
A person and a slash on the left, three brushed strokes down the right. Polishing yourself up: discipline.
A line laid over a box with a stroke through it, the same thing set out a second time. Again.
A mouth with a hand reaching up through it, holding the brush that writes it all down. History.
A worker's mark leaning over the earth: something is planted here. Exist.
A long line over a short one, standing perfectly upright. The gentleman.
A body hanging over a tangle with a tail, everything attached to the same thing. Belong.
A slash over a cloth hanging from its rail. Linen.
A heap of strokes on the left with a cloth on the right — the banner an expert leads under. The master.
Small marks over a cover, and a hanging cloth below. The everyday curtain: usual.
Ten over the sun over ten on the left, with dry on the right, straight up the middle. The trunk.
A hand on the left; on the right someone standing over a woman, the two of them meeting. Contact.
The sun on top, then a broad tangle of strokes bursting out underneath. An outburst.
Stop, with a halberd leaning across it. Arms.
Two spoons side by side, one just behind the other. Compare.
Water on the left, and on the right a bird standing over a level line. Conform.
A lid over a spray of dots with ten underneath, drawing them all in. A ratio.
Two lines with three legs hanging under them, a stone table where something is set out. Indicate.
Bamboo on top; underneath, a frame of craft-work standing on a tree. Build.
Two hooks on the left and two moons stacked on the right — the shape of what something can do. Ability.
Two hands at either side lifting the same thing, with eight underneath. Revive.
A crossroads split open, with millet growing up the middle of it. The knack of it: technique.
A wine jar on the left; on the right a lid over a slow foot. Wine gone sour: acid.
Two wings back to back, turned away from each other. Not so.
Two little uprights over a wide flat base, a row of things all standing level. And.
A lid with a bent line dropping away underneath it, gone from view. Deceased.
A person on the left; on the right a lid over sunbeams with a slash through them. A wound.
Two upright slips bound through the middle by one horizontal tie. A book.
Crossed strokes over a big one with a sword underneath — a slip cut in two so the halves have to match. A ticket.
Two hanging shapes side by side, each with a speck inside it. Eggs.
A stroke leaning over a mouth tucked underneath it. The voice behind the throne: the empress.
A line across the top with strokes hanging off it and earth at the bottom. Droop.
Three crossed lines over a big stroke with something small underneath, both hands lifted up. Play music.
Big at the top, a bird under it and a rice field at the bottom: a bird bursting up out of the field. Stirred up.
A stroke leaning over a child, keeping it going. Exist.
An old man's stooped top with a child underneath holding him up. Filial piety.
Ten with a single dot beside it, a thumb's width down from the wrist. A small measure.
A boxed shape stacked over a measure — this one job and nothing else. Exclusive.
The capital on the left with a stroke and a dot on the right, settling into place. Take up a post.
A body shape with one long leg kicked out, an arm's span used as a rule. A foot in length.
A body hanging over a tangle of strokes with a long sweep underneath, opening out. Unfold.
Three strokes bent back on themselves in a tight zigzag. Self.
Crossed strokes over a big one, wrapped round a seal at the bottom. A scroll.
Two horizontal lines with one upright through them, like a rack out in the sun. Dry.
A step on the left; on the right two little figures walking one behind the other. Follow.
A hand on the left with a halberd on the right, held out in front of you. Me.
A hand at the top, three lines through the middle and a hook below — passed down, and taken up. Acquiesce.
A hand on the left; on the right a hole with a tree under it, feeling about inside. Search.
Grass over a mouth on the left, a strike on the right, pulling you up short. Respect.
A tree on the left; on the right two little horns over a bird. Authority.
A stepped shape on the left with a weapon on the right. Steps, and a grade.
Water on the left; on the right a white square over a direction, with a strike beside it. Violent.
A tall shape with a hook to the right of it, and fire underneath. Cooked right through: ripe.
Half a tree trunk, split down the middle with only the right side kept. One-sided.
A spoon and an arrow on the left, a fork in the road on the right — stopped, not knowing which. Doubt.
A hand held flat over an eye, shading it to look into the distance. Watch over.
A stone on the left; on the right grass over two little tangles of thread. The stone that pulls: a magnet.
A husked shape on the left with a weapon on the right, beating the husks off. Cereals.
A retainer on the left, with a person over three boxes on the right, leaning down over them. Face it.
One line at the bottom with an arrow coming down to land on it. Arrive.
Grass on top; underneath, a cliff with a retainer and a halberd tucked inside it. A storehouse.
Blood on top, and a crowd of little figures underneath. The masses.
Clothes split open with a village sitting inside them. The inside, and the back.
Clothes on the left; on the right a field shape with a line down through it, patching the hole. Supplement.
A retainer and a dish on top with see underneath, looking down over the lot. Perusal.
A tangle on the left, a bowl in the middle and a village on the right — everyone home for dinner. The home town.
Grass over a mouth over a husband on the left, a small bird on the right. Difficult.
Twenty on top and a hide stretched out below it, pegged flat. Leather.
A boxed shape up top with flesh hanging underneath it. A bone.
